\section{The geometric sine correction}\label{app:geometry}

Euler's product on $|\theta|<\pi$ gives
\[
\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}=\prod_{j\ge1}
\left(1-\frac{\theta^2}{\pi^2j^2}\right).
\]
Expanding each logarithm and interchanging absolutely convergent sums yields
\[
\log\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}
=-\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\zeta(2n)}{n\pi^{2n}}\theta^{2n}.
\]
Termwise differentiation proves \eqref{eq:Gm}.  For exact-rational
certification we use $\zeta(2n)\le\zeta(2)=\pi^2/6$ and a rational lower
bound for $\pi$.  After a finite prefix, the factorial-polynomial ratio times
$(\rho/\pi)^2$ provides a contractive geometric tail.

For reference, the exact low-order suprema on $[0,\rho]$, $\rho<\pi/2$, are
bounded by
\begin{align*}
\sup\abs{\partial_\theta^2\log(\sin\theta/\theta)}
&\le \csc^2\rho-\rho^{-2},\\
\sup\abs{\partial_\theta^3\log(\sin\theta/\theta)}
&\le 2\rho^{-3}-2\cos\rho\,\csc^3\rho.
\end{align*}
The power-series majorant is less sharp but extends without a new symbolic
derivation to every order.
